items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: In real adults (CGMacros), a walk after a meal went with a rise only about 3.2 mg/dL smaller (95% CI -6.9 to 0.5): not distinguishable from zero. Your sugar rose about 14.5 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the synthetic program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL).

rejected.text: Aim to walk 10 to 20 minutes after dinner to help with your sugar. Walking after a meal went with a rise in sugar about 3.2 mg/dL smaller and your sugar rose about 14.5 mg/dL less after meals when you walked.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try to avoid eating dinner at 8 pm or later, as only 5.6% of your dinners started at this time. Sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners, so it's best to keep your dinner times earlier.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 12.8 hours of overnight fasting, with 53.3% of nights reaching 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone, in the randomized program.
